introduction: The sour or bitter taste of the food we eat is due to the presence of acids or bases in them. At this level, we learn how to identify them and understand how chemical indicators work.

core_concepts.title: Acids
core_concepts.description:
They are 'sour' in taste. 
Arrhenius Concept: They release Hydrogen ions ($H^+$) when dissolved in water. 
Everyday Examples: Lemon (Citric acid), Vinegar (Acetic acid), Curd (Lactic acid), Tamarind (Tartaric acid).

core_concepts.title: Bases and Alkalis
core_concepts.description:
They are 'bitter' in taste and feel 'soapy' to touch. 
Arrhenius Concept: They release Hydroxide ions ($OH^-$) when dissolved in water. 
Note: Bases that are highly soluble in water are called 'Alkalis' (e.g., $NaOH, KOH$). All alkalis are bases, but not all bases are alkalis. 
Everyday Examples: Soap, Baking soda, Lime water.

core_concepts.title: Indicators
core_concepts.description:
Substances that change their color or odor to indicate whether a substance is an acid or a base. 
1. Natural Indicators: Litmus (extracted from Lichen plants), Turmeric (remains yellow in acid, turns red in base). 
2. Synthetic Indicators: Phenolphthalein and Methyl Orange.

core_concepts.title: The Litmus Rule
core_concepts.description:
Acids: Turn 'Blue' litmus to 'Red'. 
Bases: Turn 'Red' litmus to 'Blue'.

important_entities.name: Ant's Sting
important_entities.significance: The sting of an ant or a bee contains 'Methanoic acid', which causes severe burning and pain. To neutralize it and get relief, a mild base like 'Baking soda' is rubbed on the stung area.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: What color is phenolphthalein in a basic solution? Students often confuse this. Phenolphthalein remains 'Colorless' in acids but turns deep 'Pink' in bases.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: BAR: Base turns red to blue. ABR: Acid turns blue to red.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Or just remember that 'B'ase makes it 'B'lue.

exam_strategy_tips: A highly repeated SSC question: 'Which acid is present in Vinegar?' Answer: Acetic acid ($CH_3COOH$).
